_comment: Every field the original's county and realm records store, and what l2-scenario does with each.
Why this file exists. Three times in one week a number a player could see was stored by
Lords2.exe, drawn by our painter and carried by our own save format, and never read out of a
.sav by l2-scenario - so a loaded game showed zero until a season ended (docs/decisions.md C142,
C153, C161). The exhaustive destructure of CountyState could not
catch any of them: a field never added to CountyState is not in the list it enumerates. So the
denominator here is the ORIGINAL'S, and nothing in it is allowed to be undecided.
One row per field. `id` is `<record>+<offset>`, the record-relative offset of element 0; `count`
and `stride` describe an array (for an array of a nested record, `stride` is that record's size).
`type` is u8, i8, u16, i16, i32 or bool (one byte, non-zero is true).
status is one of three, and there is deliberately no fourth:
imported - Scenario::kingdom holds exactly the file's bytes after a load;
derived  - the load recomputes it, and it still holds exactly the file's bytes;
excluded - not carried, and `why` says why in one line.
Checked from both sides. crates/l2-scenario/tests/stored_fields.rs requires every row to be
well formed, every field docs/records.json names to have a row of that name and width, and -
against every save on the machine - every imported and derived row to reach the kingdom holding
the file's own value. `node tools/oracle/fields.js --check` requires every offset the
decompilation reads or writes to fall inside a row, and every row to be touched by some
instruction; the same test runs it when the corpus is present.
Keyed by `id` for tools/symbols/merge-json.js. One object per line: the Rust side scans lines.
